answers.1.4: Illustration: Planners read the crack spread to judge the market margin before they set the refinery plan.
answers.2.2: Benchmark crack spreads: the market value of products made from a set ratio of crude, less the crude's price.
answers.2.3: The crude and product benchmarks of each series' recipe (the market-data module's series).
answers.2.4: The market cost of RINs, in MPC's 10-K regional and blended crack spreads.
answers.3.1: products price - crude price, for a stated crude:product ratio (for example 3-2-1)
answers.3.6: KPI-0001 is the crack-spread Genie agent's identifier for this measure. The gold table behind its metric view holds the constant KPI_ID value 'KPI Crack Spread 3-2-1' on every one of its 127 series and all 1,090,423 rows of the gold table alike, so the identifier names the measure, not a series (the decision of 2026-10-25, item 3). It keeps KPI-0001 although the module classes it as a market indicator, because the pricing assets already use it (kpi 1.3.0, the decision of 2026-10-28).
answers.4.8: MPC files crack spreads under market indicators and calls margins dependent on factors beyond its control. The list's cracks (NYMEX 3-2-1, USGC 3-2-1 MEH ex-RIN, Chicago WTI 3-2-1 ex-RIN) are benchmarks, not performance.
answers.5.3: Not realized refinery margin, not margin capture, and not MPC's R&M Margin Indicator. A 3-2-1 built from separate product and crude legs is not the published series.
answers.5.4: MPC 10 (Gulf Coast, Mid-Continent, West Coast and blended 3-2-1 cracks)
6.5: MPC's market benchmarks are the Gulf Coast, Mid-Continent and West Coast 3-2-1 crack spreads; MPC FY2025 10-K, Item 7 (reference/mpc/mpc-fy2025-10k-fact-sheet.md, section 8)
MPC states that the sweet and sour crude differentials explain why realized margin differs from the blended crack; MPC FY2025 10-K, Item 7 (reference/mpc/mpc-fy2025-10k-fact-sheet.md, section 8)
